definition: The Bulgarian Part of Speech-annotated Corpus (BulPosCor) (in Bulgarian: Български Пос анотиран корпус (БулПосКор)) is a morphologically annotated general monolingual corpus of written language where each item in a text is assigned a grammatical tag.
details: BulPosCor is created by the Department of Computational Linguistics at the Institute for Bulgarian Language of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences and consists of 174 697 lexical items. BulPosCor has been compiled from the Structured "Brown" Corpus of Bulgarian by sampling 300+ word-excerpts (expanded to sentence boundary) from the original BCB files in such a way as to preserve the BCB overall structure. The annotation process consists of a primary stage of automatically assigning tags from the Bulgarian Grammar Dictionary and a stage of manual resolving of morphological ambiguities. The disambiguated corpus consists of 174,697 lexical units.

explainer.lead: BulPosCor is a Bulgarian written-language corpus in which every lexical item carries a grammatical tag. Its 174,697 annotated items provide a compact, manually disambiguated record of Bulgarian morphology for language research and computational linguistics.

tiers.eli5: Imagine taking lots of Bulgarian sentences and putting a small grammar label on every word. BulPosCor does this for 174,697 words, with people checking cases where the automatic labels could be unclear. It helps researchers see how Bulgarian words are used in real written text.
tiers.practitioner: Each corpus item is a lexical unit with a morphological tag, produced by automatic tagging followed by manual disambiguation. The data represents general monolingual written Bulgarian and preserves the structure of the Structured "Brown" Corpus of Bulgarian, so its size and sampling design should be considered when interpreting analyses.
tiers.paperLevel: BulPosCor is a general monolingual written Bulgarian corpus comprising 174,697 morphologically annotated lexical units. Samples of 300 or more words were drawn from Structured "Brown" Corpus of Bulgarian files and expanded to sentence boundaries while preserving the corpus's overall structure; tags were assigned from the Bulgarian Grammar Dictionary and morphological ambiguities were resolved manually. Its stated scale and sampling procedure define the scope of the resource.

explainer.example: For one sample, an excerpt of at least 300 words is taken from a BCB file and extended so that it ends at a sentence boundary. Each lexical item first receives an automatic grammatical tag; annotators then manually choose the appropriate analysis wherever the automatic tagging leaves a morphological ambiguity.

usedIn.name: Bulgarian language research
usedIn.detail: Provides grammatically tagged written Bulgarian for studying word forms and their grammatical roles.

usedIn.name: Computational linguistics
usedIn.detail: Offers manually disambiguated morphological annotations for examining Bulgarian text.

explainer.measures: BulPosCor does not assign a performance score; it records the grammatical properties of each lexical item through a morphological tag. Its completed disambiguated portion contains 174,697 lexical units.

explainer.typicalResults: The resulting disambiguated corpus contains 174,697 lexical units, each associated with a grammatical tag. Its sampling preserves the overall structure of the Structured "Brown" Corpus of Bulgarian.
caveats: It contains written, monolingual Bulgarian rather than speech.
Its stated size is 174,697 lexical units.
Samples inherit the structure of the original BCB files.
